lines.text: Do you know how ads seem to follow you from site to site? Most websites quietly load code from tracking companies.
When you visit, that tracker saves a cookie in your browser: a small random ID. Think of it as a name tag.
The same tracker sits on thousands of other sites. Each visit, it reads the same name tag, and adds that page to your profile.
Even without cookies, your browser gives away clues. Screen size, fonts, time zone, graphics card. Together, they're often unique, like a fingerprint.
That profile feeds ad auctions. When a page loads, advertisers bid for your eyes, and the winner is picked in a fraction of a second.
Many browsers now block third-party cookies by default, and tracker blockers cut much of the rest.
Orbi has no accounts and no profiles. Your device just gets a random ID, and anonymous mode uses a throwaway one, so there's nothing to follow.
